statement: The Ottoman Empire's absorption of Byzantine territories occurred over a century-long process (1354–1453): Gallipoli fell (1354), Adrianople became the Ottoman capital (1365), Constantinople was surrounded on all sides after the 1390s, surviving through Timur's intervention (1402) and careful diplomacy. The final siege (1453) lasted 53 days; massive Hungarian-cast bombards breached the Theodosian Walls. Emperor Constantine XI died fighting on the walls. Mehmed II entered the city, prayed in Hagia Sophia, and proclaimed himself 'Caesar of Rome.' The fall shocked Western Christendom and ended 1,123 years of Roman imperial continuity.
